source_text:
«Ἵνα ὁ

ἄρτος οὗτος μετατραπεὶς γένηται σῶμα Χριστοῦ, σῶμα θεῖον, σῶμα σωτήριον ψυχῶν
καὶ σωμάτων, καὶ τὸ ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ τούτῳ κερασθὲν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ αἷμα Χριστοῦ, αἷμα
καινῆς διαθήκης, αἷμα σωτήριόν ἐστιν ἡμῖν, εἰς τὸ μετέχειν ἡμᾶς ὅλους τῶν ἁγίων σου
μυστηρίων ἐν καινότητι τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ οὐχὶ παλαιότητι τοῦ γράμματος».
thought_title: Prayer that the bread and cup become saving body and blood
orientation: The anaphora concludes with a petition that the consecrated bread and cup may become Christ's body and blood for the salvation and participation of the faithful.
pass_a_gloss: “So that this bread, having been changed, may become the body of Christ, a divine body, a body saving for souls and bodies, and that which has been mixed in this cup into the same thing is the blood of Christ, blood of the new covenant, blood saving for us, so that we may wholly share in your holy mysteries in newness of spirit and not in oldness of the letter.”

choices.why: The glossary requires 'changed' for this term, and the aorist passive participle needs the perfective passive sense in English.
The adjective modifies both body and blood; 'saving' keeps the active force of bringing salvation, matching the prayer's petition for souls and bodies.
This phrase indicates the mixing of the two elements into one unified substance; the literal rendering preserves the sense of convergence into a single reality.
The accusative masculine plural modifies 'us' (ἡμᾶς), emphasizing total participation of the whole person; 'wholly' captures the adverbial force.
The glossary requires this exact rendering, and it preserves the contrast with 'oldness of the letter' from the Pauline language.

bible_refs.note: ἐν καινότητι τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ οὐχὶ παλαιότητι τοῦ γράμματος

pass_b_english: May this bread be changed and become the body of Christ—a divine body, a body that brings salvation to souls and bodies. And may what has been mixed in this cup into one reality become the blood of Christ, the blood of the new covenant, blood that brings salvation to us. Grant this so that we may wholly share in your mysteries in newness of spirit, and not in the oldness of the letter.

problems.ruling: Scripture citation (Romans 7:6) absent from source; misleading addition not in Greek text.

edits.old: and not in the oldness of the letter (Romans 7:6).
edits.new: and not in the oldness of the letter.

fixed: Deleted the parenthetical citation (Romans 7:6), which is not in the source text.

problems.why: Unclear if this is still Christ's prayer, the priest's, or the compiler's; abrupt shift from narrative to petition.

problems.quote: what has been mixed in this cup into one reality
problems.why: Obscure whether 'one reality' refers to wine-water mixture or resulting sacramental presence.
problems.fix: Specify 'into one mixed reality' or 'into one sacrament'.

problems.quote: what has been mixed in this cup into one reality
problems.why: 'One reality' is vague and philosophical; the Greek likely means the mixed elements become one thing, Christ's blood.
problems.fix: Render as 'what has been mingled in this cup into one' or 'into a single offering'.

edits.new: We pray that this bread may be changed

edits.old: what has been mixed in this cup into one reality
edits.new: what has been mixed in this cup into one

fixed: The shift from narrative to petition is abrupt; adding 'We pray that' marks the prayer's voice without changing the source meaning.
The Greek 'ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ' means 'into the same thing' or 'into one'; 'into one reality' is too philosophical. Changed to 'into one' to match the source more closely.
